fixes.title: 'Best Targets Tonight' transit times are computed for the wrong night
fixes.summary: Closed by wave 3 before the verifier's bundle was built. The Best Targets provider no longer passes twilight.astronomicalDusk as the visibility `date`; it watches _currentNightDateProvider (catalog_astronomy.dart:153), which resolves the observation time through AstronomyCalculations.nightDateOf — local noon, not local midnight, is the night boundary. Re-verified here, not taken on trust.
fixes.revert_check: Reverted mosaic_targets.dart:138 from `ref.watch(_currentNightDateProvider)` to `ref.watch(_currentDateProvider)`: 'Best Targets and the Info tab agree on which night they describe' FAILED with Expected 2026-08-03 00:52:48 / Actual 2026-08-04 00:48:52 — the exact 00:48-vs-00:52 disagreement the finding reported. Restored: 5/5 pass.
fixes.caveats: The verifier lowered this to P3 (one night, ~4 min) and that correction stands.

fixes.title: RESIDUAL: the same wrong-night anchor survived at five more call sites wave 3 was fenced out of
fixes.summary: Wave 3's caveat recorded that it could only fix the Best Targets path and that other callers still handed calculateObjectVisibility a raw INSTANT. Confirmed and closed, since the fence is gone this wave. calculateObjectVisibility scans local noon to the following noon and reads only the calendar day, so any instant past midnight selects the NEXT night. Fixed: object_details_panel/content_sections.dart (the Rise/Transit/Set section at :460 and the Quick Stats transit at :850, both `date: obsTime.time`); sequencer target_queue_panel.dart:166 and target_preview_tooltip.dart:55 (both `date: now` — the queue's 'Sets' countdown read ~25h for a target an hour from the horizon when opened after midnight); full_timeline.dart's _getTargetWindows (rise/set markers off the run-start instant); plan_tonight_sequencer_helper.dart:203 (`date: window.start`, the dark window's opening instant, which falls after midnight at the west edge of a timezone in mid-summer — the finding's own scenario); and skotiq_core sequence_time_estimator.dart calculateTargetWindows, whose windows feed pre-flight's 'target sets before this block finishes' conflicts. Also repaired astronomy_calculations.dart, where wave 3 had inserted nightDateOf INSIDE calculateObjectVisibility's doc comment, orphaning half that contract doc (the paragraph defining `date`, minAltitude and standardAltitude) onto nightDateOf and leaving calculateObjectVisibility undocumented.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted `final nightDate = AstronomyCalculations.nightDateOf(date);` and put `date: nightDate` back to `date: date` in calculateTargetWindows: BOTH tests FAILED — 'a run starting after midnight is scored on the night it is IN' with Expected 2024-01-16 08:43:23 / Actual 2024-01-17 08:39:27 (a full sidereal day), and 'the night boundary is local noon, not midnight' with Expected >= 23 hours / Actual 0. Restored: 2/2 pass. Note the assertion is on riseTime/transitTime/setTime EQUALITY between a 22:00 start and a 01:00 start on the same night, so it fails if the conversion is removed anywhere in that path, not merely if a threshold moves.
fixes.caveats: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/framing/altitude_chart.dart was the sixth site on wave 3's list; a concurrent wave-4 agent had already fixed it (`date: AstronomyCalculations.nightDateOf(plottedNightMid)`), so it is untouched here. SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING DEFECT observed while probing and deliberately NOT chased, because it is a different bug and fixing it here would risk relocating this one: with host TZ -5 and longitude 0, calculateObjectVisibility returned rise=2024-01-16 08:43, transit=2024-01-15 17:50, set=2024-01-17 02:49 — a rise/set pair that neither brackets the transit nor lies inside the noon-to-noon window it claims to scan. Worth a finding of its own.
